A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, retaining the cosine classifier, PEFT ensemble, and original benchmarks despite substantial retitling and expansion. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and forgetting experiments on Split-CIFAR-100, Split-ImageNet-R, and 5-Dataset in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds evaluations of blurry tasks, output-label settings, and ensemble aggregation in Section 6 and Appendices H and J.

M1.justification: The two core methods remain, but v3 generalizes their fixed global label set to task-specific public label sets. This changes prototype initialization and updates, classifier-head dimensions, and filtering of examples outside the public labels (Sections 4.4–5). Cumulative feature sums, normalization, FiLM adaptation, and maximum-logit prediction already existed in v1.

E1.justification: All three original benchmarks and ImageNet-21K pretraining remain. Section 6.2 adds I-Blurry and SI-Blurry evaluation on CIFAR-100, extending coverage from class-disjoint tasks to recurring classes, indistinct task boundaries, and imbalanced arrivals. This substantially broadens the continual-learning conditions actually tested.

E2.justification: The Naive and full-data comparator families remain, with Full Data renamed Non CL Baseline. Appendix H.2 newly compares the proposed ArgMax aggregation with median-centered logits and Zhao et al.'s entropy-based aggregation. This is a localized expansion of evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: New experiments evaluate FiLM alongside the retained last-layer configurations on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-R, and compare task-specific 10/20-class heads with fixed 100/200-class heads. Separately, the full-data evaluation changes from training and releasing a model after every task to training one offline model on all tasks (v1 Algorithm A2; v3 Algorithm A3).

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial analyses of blurry-task robustness, public-label assumptions, last-layer versus FiLM adaptation, and ensemble aggregation rules (Figures 4–5, Appendix H.2, and Tables A3–A4). The individual-model analysis investigating the 5-Dataset ensemble anomaly in v1 Figure A.1 is removed; v3 Figure A.1 addresses aggregation instead.

E5.justification: Mean/std tables and median/min–max plots remain. CIFAR-100 reporting changes from ten seeds/repeats to five, and captions explicitly include hyperparameter-tuning variability. ImageNet-R figures report five repeats while Table A4 still specifies three seeds, leaving their run correspondence unclear. These are reported-count changes, not evidence that every retained result was rerun.

E6.justification: v3 adds FiLM, blurry-task, label-space, and aggregation results. ImageNet-R Table A4 retains the last-layer PEFT accuracy of 7.29% at epsilon = 1 and adds 33.19% for FiLM; these are different configurations. CIFAR-100 Naive accuracy at epsilon = 8 changes from 0.00% to 9.55%. The 5-Dataset final-table results remain equivalent after converting forgetting to percentages.

T1.justification: v3 adds task-wise DP and classifier-release definitions, parallel/sequential composition theorems, label-space privacy propositions, an empty-dataset counterexample, and extensive proofs and prior-definition analysis (Section 4; Appendices B–C and F). These substantially exceed v1's formal treatment. The new parallel-composition proof has a gap: Equation A17 factorizes an arbitrary joint event as a product of projected events.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on two pretrained-model approaches under assumptions S1/S2. v3 makes task-wise DP formalization, composition, and formal output-label privacy conditions central contributions. Its abstract and contribution list also explicitly extend the empirical claims to blurry tasks and alternative public-label settings.

C2.justification: v3 adds domain-shift-based guidance on when feature-only classification becomes inadequate, attributes ensemble variability to overconfidence, and explains the noise savings from task-specific public labels. It explicitly discusses restrictions on online/open-world learning and discloses that tuning privacy costs are excluded. v1's discussion of the unexplained non-DP 5-Dataset anomaly is dropped.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds FiLM parameter counts and implementation, PRV accounting, Optuna with 20 Gaussian-process tuning iterations, hyperparameter ranges, tuning/validation subsets, and batch-size/learning-rate scaling. These substantially expand v1's sparse tuning disclosure without establishing that all settings changed. Data-access instructions switch from TensorFlow Datasets to torchvision 0.18.1, and v3 adds a conditional promise of code release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v3 adds a dedicated continual-learning discussion and substantially expands positioning against prior DP-CL definitions, particularly Desai, Hassanpour, and Lai (Section 2 and Appendix B). New references cover blurry tasks, expandable adapters, streaming privacy, and adaptive composition. The relationship to prior work becomes a central theoretical argument rather than mainly contextual motivation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. Previously combined background, assumptions, and methods are reorganized into distinct sections; existing method explanations expand considerably, and appendices are reorganized around notation, theory, implementation, and results. The original 5-Dataset discussion moves mainly to the appendix.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text and references, adds the introductory privacy diagram and label-space table, and moves method algorithms into the main text. Benchmark displays are reorganized into accuracy plots and separate appendix forgetting panels, with expanded result tables and new robustness, label-space, and aggregation figures. These are substantial visual changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 directly investigates the ImageNet-R adaptation and shared-class-task limitations left unresolved in v1, strengthens practical method-selection guidance, and supplies substantially more reproducibility information. Its label-space analysis also makes privacy conditions clearer. These materially improve the paper's evidence and usefulness, although the new composition proof's general-event gap (Equation A17) and inconsistent ImageNet-R seed reporting temper the gains.
